sourceDate.text: 母憂 / 從父兄所繫之父世

translationRepairs: At the end of Song's Shengming era he began as Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, Minister of Works cavalry officer, and Central Commandant's army aide.

At the end of Song's Shengming era he entered office as an Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, cavalry officer to the Minister of Works, and aide for inner troops to the Grand Commandant.
The proposal correctly separates 太尉, Grand Commandant, from 中兵, the inner-troops staff, but the revision makes that relationship explicit and improves the list of offices.
At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and passed through Rear Army Aide, Cavalry of the Minister of Works, and Central Commandant's Army Aide.

At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and went on to serve as Rear Army Aide, Cavalry Officer to the Minister of Works, and Inner Troops Aide to the Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, while 中兵 describes the staff assignment. The revision preserves both elements of the office title in clearer literal English.
At Ying city Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guangziqin and Wu Ziyang, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
When the army reached Yingcheng, Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.
光子衿 is Guang Ziqin, not the fused Guangziqin. The revision also restores the army as the subject of 師次 and retains 等, 'and others.'
When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao rushed his men to East Yiji Gate; though shot at, he spurred forward and the bandits fled.
When bandits set fire to Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his men to answer the alarm at the East Side Gate. Though struck by an arrow, he spurred his horse forward, and the bandits turned and fled.
東掖門 is the palace's East Side Gate, not 'East Yiji Gate.' The revision also makes the sequence and the passive shooting construction natural in English.
When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to East Yiji Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to the East Side Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
掖門 is a side or flank gate of the palace. 'East Yiji Gate' is not a valid reading of 東掖門, and the proposed literal correction is accurate.
He was also made Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
He was also made General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.
鎮 in this military title is 'guard' or 'garrison.' 'General Who Guards the Army' is clearer and more idiomatic than either the original 'Pacify' or the proposal's 'Stabilizes.'
He was given the additional title Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
He was given the additional title General Who Guards the Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
The literal field should render 鎮軍將軍 consistently as General Who Guards the Army while preserving the rest of the source structure.
His father Xinbei was a Song general who rose to Pacify the Barbarians General and inspector of Xuzhou.
His father, Xinzhi, was a general under Song who rose to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Xu Province.
欣之 is Xinzhi, not Xinbei, and 征虜 is a campaigning title. The revision also renders 徐州刺史 as Inspector of Xu Province in natural English.
His father Xinbei was a Song general who reached Pacify the Barbarians General and Xuzhou Inspector.
His father Xinzhi was a Song general who reached the ranks of General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Inspector of Xu Province.
The literal translation repeats the false reading Xinbei. 欣之 is Xinzhi, and the two final phrases are the offices to which he rose.
Before he came of age, Xinbei sent him out of Xinye with one horse and a few followers; on the road several hundred Man bandits suddenly surrounded him.
Before Jingzong came of age, Xinzhi sent him out from Xinye with one horse and a few followers. On the road they were suddenly surrounded by several hundred Man bandits.
欣之 again names Xinzhi. Naming Jingzong once resolves the English pronoun chain without adding information absent from the biography.
Before he had reached the weak-crown age, Xinbei at Xinye sent him out of the province with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly met several hundred Man bandits surrounding him.

Before he had reached the age of twenty, Xinzhi sent him out of the province from Xinye with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly encountered several hundred Man bandits who surrounded him.
欣之 is Xinzhi. The revision keeps the literal structure while expressing 弱冠 as the age of twenty and placing 'from Xinye' unambiguously.

When Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen became inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians army aide and administrator of Fengyi, supervised troops south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

When Xiao Qiang, Prince of Poyang, became Inspector of Yong Province, Jingzong was again made an Inner Troops Aide to the General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Administrator of Fengyi. He supervised military affairs south of Xian and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
The proposal correctly rejects Xiao Zhen but misreads 鏘 a second time: the name is Qiang, not Jiang. The revision also parses 征虜中兵參軍 as an inner-troops staff post.

When Qi's Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen held Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians Army Aide, concurrently Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

When Qi's Prince of Poyang, Xiao Qiang, held Yong Province, Jingzong was again made Inner Troops Aide to the General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, concurrently served as Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was appointed Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
鏘 is Qiang, not Zhen or Jiang. The revised literal field preserves the source's office sequence and the structure of 征虜中兵參軍.
In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Raids General for merit.
In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Guerrilla General for merit.
遊擊將軍 is conventionally rendered Guerrilla General or General of Mobile Warfare. 'Raids General' is not an adequate rendering of the office.
Gaozu, treating him as a meritorious minister grown lax and left unpunished, summoned him to be Protector of the Army.
Because Jingzong was a meritorious minister, Gaozu shelved the case without punishing him and summoned him to serve as Protector of the Army.
寢 is transitive here: Gaozu shelved the impeachment because Jingzong was a meritorious minister. It does not say that Jingzong had grown lax.
His father's elder brother Yuanjing had been Song Grand Marshal.
His father's elder brother Yuanjing had been Song Grand Commandant.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, whereas Grand Marshal would represent 大司馬. The proposed idiomatic correction is accurate.
His father's elder brother Yuanjing was Song Grand Marshal.
His father's elder brother Yuanjing was Song Grand Commandant.
The literal field likewise needs Grand Commandant for 太尉. The proposal makes the necessary correction without altering the sentence's structure.
When the Pacification Office was established, he was made aide of the Grand Marshal.
When the hegemon's administration was established, he was appointed Attending Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.
霸府 is the pre-accession administration of the hegemon, not a Pacification Office, and 太尉 is Grand Commandant. The revision gives 從事中郎 a clearer office rendering.
When Liang arose they caught the day's last light and achieved their aims—rivaling Fang Hu and Shao Yi, their deeds cut into bell and tripod. Magnificent!

When Liang arose, they caught the dying light of the age and fulfilled their ambitions. Their deeds matched those of Fang Shu and Shao Hu, and their merits were engraved on bells and cauldrons. Magnificent indeed!
方 and 邵 are shorthand for the Zhou generals Fang Shu and Shao Hu. The revision corrects both invented names and turns the appraisal into natural English.

When the army halted at Ying city, Mao advanced and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guangziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, and decapitations numbered in the tens of thousands; he returned and presented the victory at Hanchuan.

When the army halted at Ying city, Mao advanced and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guang Ziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, and decapitations numbered in the tens of thousands; he returned and presented the victory at Hanchuan.
Independent review confirmed that 光子衿 is Guang Ziqin; the same fused name error occurred in both English fields.

In the second year of Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a supporting general and each charge broke the enemy line, with beheadings each time; by merit he was made Raids General.

In the second year of Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a supporting general and each charge broke the enemy line, with beheadings each time; by merit he was made Guerrilla General.
Independent review confirmed Guerrilla General for 遊擊將軍; the same title error occurred in both English fields.
When the Pacification Office was established, he was made Aide of the Grand Marshal.
When the hegemon's administration was established, he was made Attending Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.
Independent review confirmed that 霸府 is the hegemon's administration and 太尉 is Grand Commandant; the literal field repeated both errors.
